answer: Proof-of-Stake acts as a trellis for identity verification, requiring agents to stake collateral to harbor network influence. An attacker creating a quill of pseudonymous nodes faces linear capital costs, as each fake identity necessitates independent financial locking. By tying voting power to locked assets rather than computational volume, the system ensures that Sybil attacks remain prohibitively expensive, as the marginal cost of inflating influence scales directly with the total value at risk.
